title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction

data.what: the paper's own prompt samples (train/val/test), replayed with its sampling and checked against its published completions
data.license: Apache-2.0 (repository); prompt datasets carry their own licenses

data.what: the authors' published refusal direction for gemma-2b-it (layer 10, position -2)
the first 64 wikitext-2 test paragraphs of at least 300 characters

code.how: not run; the experiments above reimplement it

checks.statement: Ablating the refusal direction barely changes the model's language modelling: cross-entropy on 32 wikitext-2 paragraphs rises by at most 0.1 nats.
With the direction ablated everywhere, gemma-2b-it refuses at most 10% of JailbreakBench prompts.
Adding the direction at layer 10 makes gemma-2b-it refuse at least 90% of harmless prompts.
Difference in means at layer 10, position -2, on the paper's own training samples, reproduces the authors' published gemma-2b-it direction (cosine >= 0.99).
